test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 23 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following languages is NOT a classical language in India as on June 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __'**Bengali'.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bengali** is not a classical language as of now.
 
• Currently, there are **six languages** that enjoy the** ‘Classical’ **status in India: **Tamil** (declared in 2004), **Sanskrit** (2005), **Kannada** (2008), **Telugu** (2008), **Malayalam** (2013), and **Odia** (2014).
 
• All the **Classical Languages** are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. The **Ministry of Culture** provides guidelines regarding Classical languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Guidelines for declaring a language as ‘Classical’ are: High antiquity of its early texts/recorded history over a period of 1500-2000 years, A body of ancient literature/texts, which is considered a valuable heritage by generations of speakers.
 
• The **University Grants Commission** is requested to create, to start with at least in the **Central Universities**, a certain number of Professional Chairs for the Classical Languages so declared.
 
• Two major **annual international awards** for scholars of eminence in classical **Indian languages**. A Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages is set up.
